question: Why are German pretzels dipped in a bath of lye before they are baked?
answer: To make the Maillard reaction run fast. Browning speeds up in alkaline conditions, because the amino groups that react with sugars stay free instead of being tied up by acid. A dip in 3 to 4% sodium hydroxide gives a mahogany crust in minutes; baking turns the lye into milder sodium carbonate.
move: Change the conditions and the same reaction can run many times faster.
ask: What small change could make something slow in my life move much faster?
source: Martins et al., Trends Food Sci. Technol., 2000
reference: Martins, Jongen & van Boekel, A review of Maillard reaction in food and implications to kinetic modelling, Trends in Food Science & Technology, 2000
